messages.author: 333f3e76f253995a
messages.subject: Importing outlines
parts:
Dear list, I'm trying to import an outline to geomorph. I followed the instructions in geomorph quick guide without success. First, I get the outline using as template the closest specimen to consensus and save it in tps format. Then, the steps I followed are, 1) calculate the mean shape of raw data, ref <- mshape(rawdata); 2) Get the specimen used as template, sp6 <- rawdata[,,6]; 3) Run function to create mean shape outline, ms_outline <- warpRefOutline("outline_sp6.tps", sp6, ref). This last command shows a plot with the imported outline and the warped outline, but I noticed that the last one is in the same coordinates as the imported outline (jpeg attached). As in the quick guide example, I think that the warped outline must be centered?.  When trying to use the outline e.g. in plotRefToTarget, the outline is not shown.
Thanks in advance,
Alejo

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: Importing outlines
parts:
Dear Alejo,

The issue is that you are making ref, the mean shape, from the raw data. This should be the mean of the Procrustes shape residuals - then it will be centered as in the example.

Emma

Check the input objects, (the file with the outline points, the raw coordinates of closest specimen to mean shape (3d array), and the mean shape of Procrustes residuals (also a 3d array). In my case, the outline file was made in tpsdig, with the "draw background curves" tool, taking into account the scale, and the only curve captured was resampled by length with many points. 
Regards,

Alejo

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: Importing outlines
parts:
Dear Giselle,

As Alejo said, you must make sure you use the raw (pre GPA) landmarks that correspond to the specimen and the outline (and these should line up if plotted in R), and the mean Procrustes residuals for ref.

Your issue sounds like your matrices of coordinates are not numerical. 

Emma
